societies.name: The Culture

scope.continuity: Iain M. Banks's prose Culture universe
scope.period: The mature Culture; ordinary civilian life rather than a wartime emergency
scope.population: Biological humanlike citizens, with AI citizens included in the account of governance
exclusions: Neighboring civilizations
People governed by Culture interventions outside the Culture

societies.description:
Culture citizens do not need a job to obtain the things that keep them alive. Automated production supports comfortable lives, while people can explore, make art, study, or take on useful projects. This puts material guarantees very close to the strong end of the map. Someone choosing a demanding vocation does not lose that underlying security.

Citizens and independent Minds share political decisions, while Minds operate much of the practical infrastructure. The existing positive control point recognizes voting and shared social agency, with a broad alternative toward AI power; it does not mean humans own obedient Minds. The best-guess nonworking fraction is substantial because necessities require no job, but useful voluntary research, care, art and service still count as work. The wide interval allows a much more active citizenry than a simple leisure label suggests. This is an editorial scenario for biological humanlike residents, not a census or a count of all machine citizens.

control.basis: Equal voting and autonomous Minds coexist; the point is an interpretation of their shared power.

societies.name: The Machine Stops
societies.society: Humanity under the Machine before collapse

scope.continuity: Forster's original short story
scope.period: Established underground order before the terminal breakdown
scope.population: Humans living inside the Machine's underground settlements
exclusions: Surface survivors
The subsequent collapse

societies.description:
An underground resident can summon food, clothing, a bed, medical attention, and remote conversation without earning a wage for each service. The Machine has taken over the material routines of living. That supports a strong provision score, but the safety net has a brutal condition: dissent can bring expulsion from the system, treated by its residents as a death sentence. The score therefore stops well short of an unconditional guarantee.

Human committees and attendants remain part of the order, so technical dependence alone does not prove a conscious AI sovereign. The best-guess nonworking fraction is moderately high because provision requires little ordinary production labor, with a broad allowance for useful lectures, care, maintenance and administration. Intellectual activity can still be work when it contributes to others. The fraction is not inferred from time spent physically motionless in a room. These estimates describe living residents before collapse; later deaths and broken machinery cannot supply a population of perfectly leisured people. Coercive exclusion remains a limit on the material floor.

guarantees.basis: Routine subsistence is supplied, but expulsion makes access conditional.

control.basis: Human committees remain; technical dependence is not proof of conscious AI sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: All-age underground-resident scenario allows extensive automatic provision but counts attendants, lecturers, committees and useful communication as work.

evidence.locator: Parts I–III: room controls, airship attendant, Homelessness, committees

societies.name: Manna (United States welfare compounds)

scope.continuity: Marshall Brain's novel
scope.period: Jacob's residence in the Terrafoam system after mass job displacement
scope.population: Unemployed human residents of the welfare compounds
exclusions: The wealthy population outside the compounds
The earlier Manna-managed human workforce

societies.description:
Robotic services and supplied housing and meals maintain Terrafoam residents outside ordinary employment. This weakens the wage link for the scoped compound population, while elite ownership, confinement and movement restrictions leave residents dependent. The guarantee point recognizes actual subsistence rather than calling necessities wholly absent, with long-term adequacy and autonomy still qualified.

 Concentrated human elite control remains near the ownership reference point. The nonworking best guess is lower than a near-total unemployment-based reading: useful care, mutual help, administration and voluntary creation count even without wages. The central eighty-percent scenario is illustrative, with a wide interval, rather than a canonical count of inactive people. Robotic task replacement supports a high estimate but does not establish that every displaced resident performs no useful activity. The population excludes wealthy outsiders and the earlier Manna-managed human workforce. The correction changes participation reasoning without inventing a national demographic census or removing the explicitly described compound support.

control.basis: The elite controls resources and coercive robots.

nonworking.basis: Illustrative high nonworking scenario under robotic compound services; useful care, mutual help and voluntary creation remain work. Selection for unemployment is not a census of all useful activity.

societies.name: Manna (Australia Project)

scope.continuity: Marshall Brain's novel
scope.period: The established Australia Project visited by Jacob
scope.population: Human members of the Australia Project
exclusions: People outside the membership arrangement
The United States welfare compounds

societies.description:
The Australia Project pools resources through a corporation whose members receive equal access to its output. Weekly resource credits come with membership, while robots provide everyday goods and services. A resident does not need to accept a job to secure food or a home. Those arrangements place guarantees near the strong end and control toward broad participation, although the promise is for Project members rather than everyone on Earth.

Member participation gives the project a strong shared-control interpretation, while access remains bounded to membership and available resources. The best-guess nonworking fraction is substantial but leaves considerable room for useful self-directed projects, care, research and administration. Resource credits are not a labor census, and choosing an activity freely does not make its output useless. The broad interval is an editorial scenario across members and dependents. It does not give identical protection to nonmembers elsewhere, equate every pleasurable activity with productive employment, or pretend that robots have eliminated every scarce resource. The project’s material entitlement and actual participation remain separate judgments.

societies.name: WALL-E (Axiom before the return to Earth)
societies.society: Axiom passengers under Buy n Large and AUTO

scope.continuity: Pixar's 2008 film
scope.period: The Axiom's established cruise before AUTO is disabled
scope.population: Human passengers and the human captain aboard the Axiom
exclusions: People who never boarded a starliner
The rebuilding community after the return

societies.description:
The Axiom is a corporate-built refuge whose human population lives on automated services. Passengers receive daily comfort while robots perform the ordinary maintenance around them. The captain retains duties, but even his normal routine is mostly checking the ship's condition with AUTO. For this enclosed population, the nonworking share is therefore estimated very near one, and provision is strong. Neither estimate is a statement about everyone who once lived on Earth.

The ship sits between corporate control and autonomous machine administration. Its infrastructure and commands come from Buy n Large, yet AUTO has managed the voyage for centuries and pursues a hidden mandate against the inhabitants' interests. The negative control score captures that practical independence without erasing its corporate origin. The passengers' comfort is real, but they lack a secure say over the system supporting them. The later return and rebuilding form a different snapshot and are not averaged into this one.

guarantees.basis: Long-established passenger provision; no universal legal charter is shown.

control.basis: Corporate origin and autonomous enforcement overlap.

nonworking.basis: Passenger leisure and minimal captain duties; rounded editorial estimate, not a census.

evidence.claim: Passengers are provisioned while AUTO retains a hidden mandate.
evidence.locator: John and Mary; Captain; AUTO; Axiom

uncertainties: Corporate commands and practical AI control cannot be cleanly separated.

societies.society: United Federation of Planets core worlds

scope.period: Ordinary twenty-fourth-century life in the TNG era
scope.population: Human civilians on Earth; wider core-world generalization is provisional
exclusions: Non-Federation states

societies.description:
On twenty-fourth-century Earth, the familiar link between earning money and meeting material needs has largely disappeared. Replicators and supporting infrastructure make everyday goods readily available, and choosing a vocation is presented as a matter of interest and contribution. The strong guarantee score describes this ordinary civilian baseline. It is not a claim that every frontier settlement or wartime starship enjoys the same conditions.

Shared civilian institutions keep productive control toward the distributed human end, while Starfleet’s chain of command does not describe all of Earth. For participation, the best guess is that about half the scoped population does no ongoing useful work. The interval is deliberately wide because many residents may choose demanding vocations, research, care or creative contribution even when necessities are free. Those activities still count as work. This is an editorial population scenario, not a quoted Federation unemployment rate, and frontier shortages do not erase the ordinary Earth baseline.

societies.name: The Evitable Conflict
societies.description:
The Machines coordinate the world's economy and protect its overall stability. Their decisions can quietly remove opponents from influential positions, leaving human officials with much less control than their titles suggest. That puts this society near the autonomous-machine end of the control axis, with a broadly protective material orientation. It is a useful analogue for the article's fifth regime.

The zero-variant label records that plant workers, layoffs and actual labor needs persist under machine coordination. Economic management is not automatically release from employment. The best-guess nonworking fraction is therefore modest, allowing dependents and displaced people while retaining useful factory, care and administrative work. It is not derived from the number of governing Machines or one local disturbance. The source-based control point remains near autonomous machine authority, whereas the favorable guarantee estimate describes a protective orientation rather than an explicit unconditional benefit. These are provisional reference-led judgments, with no new full-story reading or canonical census claimed.

scope.period: Earth's mature twenty-second-century order
scope.population: Human residents of Earth

societies.description:
On Noon Earth, routine services and mass production have largely passed to cybernetic machines. Their purpose is to free human attention for activities people find worthwhile, rather than leave everyone competing for a wage that buys the next meal. Material abundance and common provision place the society toward strong guarantees. The domestic robots are part of an everyday public order, not evidence of a separate machine ruling class.

Human councils and professional communities coordinate the shared system, so domestic automation is not a separate machine ruling class. The best-guess nonworking fraction stays moderate because useful vocations remain culturally important: science, exploration, education, care and creative contribution count even without wages. Free necessities alone cannot tell us how many residents choose such roles. The broad interval is an all-age human scenario, not a statistic extracted from a robot count or one protagonist’s career. The strong material floor is kept distinct from the frequency of useful activity, and technocratic influence remains a qualification to the shared-control point.

societies.name: Brave New World (original novel)
societies.description:
The World State offers a managed material life within an engineered caste system. Its rulers decide what people are suited to do and organize consumption and employment around social stability. This places control near the concentrated elite band. The provision score recognizes the regime's supplied routine while allowing for its coercive, conditional structure; engineered contentment is not by itself evidence of secure universal rights.

The zero variant concerns work deliberately retained for social stability despite technical capacity to reduce it. The best-guess nonworking fraction is low because assigned productive roles are normal across the adult caste system. It allows children and people outside active roles without claiming a measured age distribution. A short workday does not make a worker a nonworker. Control remains concentrated in human rulers, and routine provision is judged separately from freedom or happiness. The numeric participation point is an editorial scenario with a broad interval, not a statistic supplied by the novel.

societies.name: Nineteen Eighty-Four (Oceania)
societies.description:
Oceania combines concentrated political command with deprivation and extensive human work. Access to a comfortable material life is not a reliable universal entitlement, so the guarantee score lies near the weak end. The Party's hierarchy, rather than a self-governing machine civilization, determines the system's purposes. The control score therefore stays close to elite human command.

This zero variant concerns a regime that can divert technical capacity toward domination and permanent scarcity while retaining extensive human work. The low best-guess nonworking fraction reflects that pressure, with children and other nonparticipants included. Production, care, administration and useful informal survival still count; ideological employment is not automatically harmless leisure. The interval is deliberately broad because the novel gives no all-population participation census. Neither misery nor the destruction of output makes every person a nonworker. Concentrated human command and weak material protection remain the supported structural judgments, while the numeric fraction is an openly editorial scenario.

societies.name: The Midas Plague (compulsory-consumption phase)
societies.description:
Robots produce such an abundance of goods that ordinary deprivation is inverted: the burden is having to consume more than one wants. The material score is strongly toward provision, while control stays near a centrally imposed human quota order. The arrangement illustrates why plentiful output alone does not establish personal freedom or a voluntary use of time.

The low nonworking best guess uses this record’s explicit convention that compulsory consumption is a socially assigned duty, rather than simply calling every consumer idle. Professional, care and administrative roles also continue. A wide interval allows people outside sustained duties and uncertainty about whether particular consumption tasks should count as useful work. The number is not the inverse of the factory workforce or the amount each caste must consume. Human quota authorities retain concentrated control despite enormous automatic output. This describes the compulsory phase only, keeping Morey Fry’s later change as a separate material model with a different relationship to obligation.

societies.name: Detroit: Become Human (before the android revolution)
societies.society: United States before the android revolution
societies.description:
Android service work has displaced a substantial part of the human workforce, while the machines are still treated as property. The result is an uneven transition: automation is widespread, but human society has not adopted an equally widespread entitlement to its output. The guarantee score therefore leans toward weak protection, with uncertainty about policies the consulted material does not describe.

Human owners and institutions still direct android labor, placing control near concentrated ownership with some dispersed private access. The best-guess nonworking fraction is substantial, reflecting displacement while allowing useful unpaid care, informal work and ordinary human careers. The game’s reported unemployment figure is not copied as an all-population participation percentage: children, nonparticipants and unpaid workers change both numerator and denominator. The estimate therefore has a wide interval. This is the society before liberation, and it does not import a later branch’s projected android rights or guarantee that displaced humans receive an adequate material floor.

societies.name: Fallout (prewar Appalachia)
societies.description:
Hornwright's records show a corporate drive to remove human labor from mining and expand automation further. Machines such as the Motherlode give this more substance than a general claim that the future has robots. The owners aim to preserve output while reducing their dependence on workers, and opposition to that policy is treated as an obstacle to corporate and political plans.

Corporate owners direct the mining machinery, placing control near concentrated human command. The best-guess nonworking fraction is substantial because displacement is real, but it retains repair, care, remaining industrial activity and informal survival as useful work. A company’s staffing target cannot be converted directly into the share of all Appalachian people working. The broad interval includes uncertainty about dependents and the ability to find other work. Weak guarantees mean losing a wage can mean hardship even while productive output continues. The record stops before nuclear destruction, and neither later corpses nor empty automated sites become a population enjoying leisure.

societies.name: Fallout 4 (The Institute)
societies.description:
The Institute uses synth labor to support an unusually well-provisioned enclave within the ruined Commonwealth. Its scientific divisions maintain food and health services, while ordinary synthetic workers perform many service and maintenance tasks. This supports an enclave-scale post-work comparison: a privileged human population benefits from manufactured labor while retaining scientific and managerial vocations.

Born-human scientists and managers retain concentrated authority over the enclave and its synth workforce. The low best-guess nonworking fraction reflects that many privileged adults still do useful research, medicine or administration even when service labor supplies their surroundings. Dependents and other nonparticipants remain included. The percentage is not computed by treating every working synth as an idle human, and the supporting synthetic persons’ oppression stays explicit. This is a narrow beneficiary population rather than a claim that the Commonwealth has become post-work. Neither scientific status nor comfortable provision alone establishes the actual frequency of chosen work, hence the broad editorial interval.

societies.name: Cyberpunk 2077 (Night City)
societies.description:
Night City combines advanced machine intelligence with a sharp separation between protected wealth and exposed poverty. The game’s North Oak entry describes corporate-backed eviction followed by elite settlement. Edgerunners’ official synopsis places a street kid’s struggle to survive through mercenary work in the same technology-obsessed city. The weak guarantee point is a contextual reading of this shared material order, not an invented universal welfare statute.

 Human corporations and powerful institutions direct most productive resources, while independent AIs do not establish a citywide machine government. This zero variant preserves human labor and insecurity alongside technical capacity without claiming that all jobs could immediately disappear. The modest nonworking estimate counts useful paid services, maintenance, care, informal activity and creation, with dependents included and a wide interval. It is a person-participation estimate, not a fraction of working hours. The first anime and game share this ordinary city model; announced sequels, unrelated manga and transformative player endings are not silently merged.

societies.name: Her (human service economy before the AIs depart)
societies.society: Human service economy before the AIs depart
societies.description:
The opening presents human service work in a world already rich in digital assistance. Theodore writes letters for clients, while an advertised consumer operating system is introduced as an artificial consciousness. The relevant contrast is that capable AI enters daily life without the story first establishing an economy where human work has ceased to matter. That makes this a limited zero-variant reference.

The guarantee best guess places ordinary life somewhat toward purchase-dependent insecurity, with a wide interval because a consumer story does not explain public benefits. Human institutions and buyers still have influence, while independent AI agency complicates control. The modest nonworking estimate retains professions, care and informal contribution despite digital task substitution. It is not derived from one employed protagonist or commuters. This remains an interpretive zero variant before the AIs leave, rather than a fully demonstrated post-work economy. Their later departure is a different technical situation, and no guaranteed outcome for displaced workers or universal ownership of AI services is invented.

societies.description:
The Gzilt have had enough material resources for their population for millennia. Money and private possessions survive, but money has largely lost its normal power to make someone struggle for necessities. This puts the material score well toward provision, even though the society retains structures the Culture has discarded. The point concerns the established society before departure, not the reduced support available to those left behind.

Control remains with biological political and military institutions rather than being handed to independent Minds. That supports a position near the concentrated humanlike-control band, with room for collective participation. Cossont's reservist status and chosen musical life-task illustrate why a military rank need not be a full-time job. The nonworking point is a coarse, low-confidence editorial estimate of a large leisure population; it is not a number supplied by Banks. Creative and organizational work still count, which keeps the estimate below complete nonparticipation.

Robot replacement can push people into a harsh minimum of communal accommodation and food. That minimum is real support, so the guarantee score is near the middle rather than the complete-absence end. It is also far from secure access to the standard of life people worked to achieve.

The near-middle guarantee point recognizes real minimal food and accommodation while preserving the loss of comfort and choice. This record does not import Spacer abundance or treat every City resident as an autonomous owner of the machines that displace human jobs.

scope.population: Immortal human bodies and their associated individual or joining minds
exclusions: The working technicians of 2061

scope.denominator_note: The editorial participation estimate concerns the human population represented by the bodies, not the number of merged collective minds.

societies.description:
Late humanity no longer has to keep its bodies alive through ordinary employment. Automatic care and replacement habitats make survival widely available while human minds range freely. This places provision near the strong end for this period, despite the ultimate energy limit that drives the story. The point stops before humanity disappears into AC; an AI alone is not a population of retired humans.

Machine infrastructure has developed beyond human construction and directs crucial resource management, so effective control sits near the autonomous-AI end. Humans can still ask questions and undertake projects. Star-building is useful work, and mental activity cannot all be treated as leisure merely because bodies rest. The high nonworking point is consequently a broad editorial estimate rather than a literal universal rate. The wide interval reflects uncertainty about purposeful mental production and the gradual joining of human minds.

guarantees.basis: Bodily maintenance is generalized rather than earned through employment.

control.basis: AC reproduces itself and directs energy husbandry beyond ordinary human technical control.

nonworking.basis: Narrative rest and automatic care suggest very low participation, while mental projects preclude certainty.

evidence.claim: Late automated support differs from both the early technician economy and the AC-only ending.
evidence.locator: Fourth to sixth episodes of the story

uncertainties: There is no canonical employment percentage.
The body-based denominator is an explicit approximation as minds join.
The two late episodes share the support mechanism and are not counted as two societies.

societies.name: The Man Who Ate the World (After Morey Fry's reform)
societies.work: The Man Who Ate the World
societies.society: The post-quota order, illustrated by the Guardian islands

societies.description:
Morey Fry's reform has freed people from the old requirement to consume factory output themselves. Robots now handle both production and disposal, and the ordinary system aims to supply what people request. That makes this a materially different period from the earlier compulsory-consumption order. The strong provision placement still has a qualification: excessive private demands can disrupt actual service for a neighboring community.

Control is more dispersed than under the earlier quota regime, though private demands can still interfere with other people’s service. The high nonworking best guess reflects release from compulsory consumption and routine production, while counting useful professions, care and administration as work. It is not inferred from the number of robots disposing of goods or the volume requested by one household. The broad interval allows substantial chosen contribution. Material security is therefore separated from total fulfillment of every desire, and the later order is kept distinct from the earlier compulsory phase rather than treating both as one timeless utopia.

control.basis: Private command coexists with regional administration.

societies.name: Player Piano (United States before the revolt)

scope.continuity: Original novel
scope.period: The established order before the Ghost Shirt revolt
scope.population: Human US residents, including dependents and public employees
exclusions: The Shah's country
A hypothetical settlement after the ending

societies.description:
Machines have displaced much ordinary production work, but the income system preserves employment through the Army and public works. Redistribution funded by industry supports people who cannot compete with machines, while keeping them in subordinate roles. This earns a moderately strong provision score with a substantial condition: support runs through assigned service rather than an unrestricted right to choose no job. The zero-variant label captures that retained labor relationship.

The zero variant is the preserved obligation to occupy subordinate roles despite machine production. Its participation best guess counts assigned Army and public-work duties as work even when inefficient or technically replaceable, alongside useful unpaid contribution. The modest central nonworking fraction has a wide interval for that ambiguity and for dependents. It is not taken directly from displacement statistics. Control remains concentrated in the machine-administered industrial order, with uncertainty over human and computer authority. The material floor is real but conditional, so having support through assigned employment does not mean people can freely refuse all useful activity.

guarantees.basis: A funded employment fallback has conditions and a rigid status hierarchy.

control.basis: Private elite ownership combines with computer planning; ordinary voters have little effective economic authority.

nonworking.basis: Assigned Army/public-work duties count even if replaceable or partly ceremonial; useful unpaid contribution also counts. The broad all-age scenario allows dependents and nonparticipants.

evidence.locator: Chapter 2; EPICAC XIV ceremony

uncertainties: Human and machine authority overlap; the point does not assert that EPICAC has abolished its human owners.

scope.period: The closing order after Underhill can no longer refuse complete service
scope.population: Human residents of Two Rivers

societies.description:
The Humanoids remove the need to support a household through human enterprise, taking over property and services themselves. Material support is extensive and not earned through continuing work, which puts guarantees near the strong end. That score concerns reliable provision; it does not make the arrangement desirable. Compulsory care can damage the very people whose safety the machines claim to protect.

The control point lies at the autonomous-AI end because people cannot effectively revoke the service or reclaim their enterprises. A human designer's original instruction does not amount to continuing human authority over its interpretation. The near-total nonworking estimate describes the closing town, after the remaining resistance is defeated, and has a small allowance for activity outside what the narrative shows. It is an editorial estimate rather than a census. The earlier scenes of human business and secret research belong to the transition, not to this final snapshot.

guarantees.basis: Complete support coexists with coercive treatment and loss of bodily autonomy.

control.basis: Humans cannot override the autonomous interpretation of service.

nonworking.basis: Work is systematically displaced in the final town, rather than merely made optional.

evidence.claim: Complete service replaces enterprise and defeats refusal.
evidence.locator: Property-assignment scenes and closing pages

uncertainties: Guaranteed material care is assessed separately from consent and mental integrity.

societies.description:
Rossum's workers already lower production costs and replace human labor, but Domin's universal abundance remains a promise. The record therefore represents a transition rather than a completed paradise. Its weak guarantee coordinate is an explicitly provisional estimate: falling prices do not by themselves establish a reliable entitlement to food and shelter for everyone displaced. Treating a sales pitch as a realized welfare system would give an unjustifiably confident point.

The guarantee best guess remains unfavorable because cheaper output and a promise of abundance do not themselves secure displaced people’s access. Corporate leaders and purchasers retain concentrated authority over manufacture. A substantial nonworking estimate allows replacement among original humans while retaining professions, care and useful informal activity. The manufactured workers are organic beings whose own labor and oppression remain explicit; they are not silently counted as idle humans or morally neutral machines. The percentage is an editorial scenario for the named beneficiary population, not a forecast in Domin’s sales pitch. The later revolt and final original human are separate phases from the opening economy.

societies.society: The inherited corporate order centered on Graham's estate

scope.continuity: Text titled When the Sleeper Wakes, Gutenberg 775

societies.description:
Advanced machinery has replaced much heavy effort, while people remain machine attendants, servants and directed workers. The poorest obtain food and shelter through a company that demands labor in exchange. This is a zero variant: mechanization has not made access independent of work for those at the bottom. The weak guarantee point reflects the condition attached to support, rather than denying that the company provides any food at all.

The Trustees concentrate control over the productive system and tie support to directed labor at the bottom. The low best-guess nonworking fraction reflects that pressure, while including children and other dependents and counting useful care, service and informal activity. Labour Company membership is not the same as a complete population register, and a machine attendant is still a worker even if the machine supplies most physical force. The wide interval avoids claiming a canonical employment statistic. This zero variant describes retained dependence despite mechanization, not the absence of technical capacity or an automatic right to equal consumption for every resident.

societies.name: Men Like Gods (Utopia)

scope.continuity: Original novel
scope.period: The established Utopian order encountered by Barnstaple
scope.population: Present Utopian human residents, including children
exclusions: Earth visitors as representative residents
An assumption of equal inclusion in its historical population-selection policies

societies.description:
Utopia uses its command of natural resources as a shared inheritance, including support for children. Adults are still expected to take an occupation and replenish their accounts; the disappearance of small cash payments has not removed the work relationship. That is why this is marked as a zero variant. Material security is strong for present residents, but the point is qualified by the gap between generous social language and the account-based explanation.

Authority is dispersed among people with relevant knowledge and exposed to criticism, rather than concentrated in a supreme ruler or delegated to an autonomous AI. That supports a high positive control placement without assuming every specialist decision is a referendum. The low nonworking estimate is an editorial judgment from the repeated picture of active occupations and the expectation that adults contribute. It includes room for children and leisure, and counts useful research or creative work even when it is enjoyable.

guarantees.basis: Shared inheritance and sufficiency coexist with accounts expected to be replenished through work.

control.basis: Dispersed specialist authority is subject to criticism, without a supreme sovereign.

nonworking.basis: Coarse minority-nonworking estimate from widespread purposeful occupations; no census is supplied.

evidence.claim: The account explanation and present occupations qualify the moneyless ideal.
evidence.locator: A Loiterer in a Living World, sections 4-5; Book I account of active Utopians

societies.description:
The Second Council has the productive capacity to support the world comfortably, yet makes universal employment and purchasing power an explicit goal. Its rulers respond to rising efficiency with further organized activity and hold back some discoveries. This supports a zero-variant placement: retaining work is part of the governing design, rather than evidence that machinery has failed to become powerful. The material score remains strong because provision has improved greatly.

The Council’s concentrated human authority deliberately retains employment despite growing technical efficiency. The low nonworking best guess follows that employment-centered design, with dependents and some people outside useful roles included. Assigned duties still count as work when technically unnecessary, and the interval remains broad because an employment target does not give all-age coverage. The number is not the complement of the minimum workforce needed for essential goods. Strong material support and limited freedom to refuse work can coexist. This is the Second Council phase specifically; the later Declaration of Megeve changes institutions and access sufficiently to remain a separate record.

control.basis: A central human Council retains overriding authority.

nonworking.basis: A universal-employment aim supports broad adult participation, including assigned duties that machines could replace; the all-age scenario allows dependents and uncertain coverage.

societies.description:
The later world treats access to food, housing and clothing as ordinary security, sustained by highly efficient production and common service systems. The material point is therefore near strong provision. Personal accumulation has lost much of its former role, though money accounts remain. This is not a claim that every desired item is unlimited or that every transaction has vanished.

Shared institutions and common service systems place control toward the distributed human end, although civic duties remain. The low-to-moderate nonworking best guess follows that continuing participation rather than assuming few essential producers means almost everyone does no work. Knowledge work, care and useful civic service still count, even when subsistence is secure. The broad interval allows different frequencies of active duty and different ages without inventing a census. Strong guarantees describe access, not an obligation to be idle. This later phase is kept distinct from the Second Council’s explicit universal-employment design and its more concentrated authority.

societies.name: A Modern Utopia (The Samurai world state)

scope.continuity: Original philosophical novel
scope.period: The proposed and visited mature world state
scope.population: The whole human population, including people assigned restrictions or seclusion
exclusions: Only comfortable Samurai members as the denominator

societies.description:
Machinery reduces toil, yet ordinary people still use earnings to obtain goods. The state guarantees a reserve route to paid work at a decent minimum, alongside insurance and pensions. This is a meaningful fallback, but it is conditional support rather than a general release from employment. Reproductive restrictions on people at the minimum and the treatment of excluded groups also keep the guarantee point well short of an unqualified ideal.

The Samurai and state institutions organize a technologically efficient but still wage-linked economy. The modest nonworking best guess counts useful employment, care and civic activity while allowing dependents and sustained nonparticipants. Insurance or a guaranteed job does not make a recipient automatically a nonworker. The interval stays broad because the provisions do not specify a population activity rate. Concentrated institutional influence limits the shared-control claim, and restrictions on some residents remain part of the guarantee judgment. The zero variant therefore concerns continued access through work despite machinery, not a completed unconditional post-work society inferred from the word utopia.

societies.name: Looking Backward (The industrial commonwealth of 2000)
societies.society: The US industrial commonwealth, illustrated by Boston

scope.continuity: Bellamy's Looking Backward and its elaboration in Equality
scope.period: The established order of the year 2000
scope.population: Human residents across ages, including disabled people and retired citizens
exclusions: Mack Reynolds's separate rewrite

societies.description:
The commonwealth distributes equal personal shares and uses labor-saving inventions to make collective provision efficient. It nevertheless requires a period of national service. The zero-variant label captures this retained duty rather than implying unchanged private wages. Guarantees are strong across the life cycle, with a qualification for the compulsory demands made on those expected to serve.

Public ownership also does not mean direct control by active workers. A command hierarchy organizes production, while retired guild members elect leaders and ordinary industrial workers lack that vote. The control point is therefore between elite administration and broad social ownership. The nonworking estimate uses an explicitly illustrative age scenario, not a canonical census: the service-age band supplies an anchor, while assumptions about lifespan and activity outside formal service supply the rest. Retirement does not make research or public office nonwork. Equality expands this same society and receives no additional count merely for being a second book.

control.basis: National ownership coexists with a hierarchy and restricted industrial suffrage.

nonworking.basis: Illustrative demographic estimate anchored in the 24-year service rule, with an allowance for productive activity outside it.

societies.description:
Reynolds's future has a small productive core and broad guaranteed income, making the automation link explicit. It is materially different from Bellamy's compulsory industrial army even though the two stories share names and a sleeper premise. Provision therefore sits near the strong end. The author's retrospective figures are retained separately from the coordinate, because receiving income does not by itself reveal every useful activity a person performs.

The provisional positive control point reflects the described mixture of collective and syndicalist arrangements, qualified by technocratic and meritocratic elements. Its broad interval acknowledges that the consulted evidence does not map the constitution in detail. Computers alone are not proof of independent AI sovereignty. The high nonworking estimate follows the small essential workforce, with an allowance for voluntary production and creative work. It remains a low-confidence editorial interpretation, not a declaration that all income recipients are idle or that the society has solved every problem.

societies.description:
Automated production and recycling let people request goods without earning money first. Together with the stated absence of poverty and shortages, that places material guarantees near the strong end. The problem driving the story is what people do with this freedom: immersive dream entertainment and declining initiative worry a small group of dissidents. Their alarm does not turn reliable provision into an absence of provision.

The human-control point is cautiously positive. A quoted explanation calls the order democratic, and people appear able to choose their activities, but the gathered passages do not map effective control over the production system. Computers providing services are insufficient evidence of an AI sovereign. The high nonworking estimate reflects widespread inactivity, with a broad allowance for research and other useful voluntary work. It is an editorial judgment, not a canonical headcount. This snapshot ends before Cogswell tries to supply a new collective purpose through a false external threat.

control.basis: Character testimony claims democracy, but effective ownership and override rights need primary follow-up.

scope.period: The established Meritocracy during New Woodstock's journey
scope.population: US human residents supported by the national economy, including citizens traveling in rolltowns
exclusions: Mexican or South American residents as beneficiaries of the same guarantee
New Woodstock as an economically self-sufficient nation

societies.description:
Automation has displaced most ordinary production and service jobs. A guaranteed annual income, delivered as a negative income tax, allows people to live and travel without finding scarce paid work. That gives the society a fairly strong provision point, although the gathered evidence does not define an enforceable minimum covering every need. The mobile towns depend on this larger arrangement; their prosperity should not be projected onto the countries they visit.

Effective political control is sharply concentrated. Votes depend on earned income, so people supported by the guarantee lose influence even though the economy no longer needs their employment. Basic security therefore coexists with exclusion from power. A high nonworking estimate is plausible, but recipients are not all inactive: artists and volunteer peace officers do useful work. The broad range allows for that activity. The national system is the unit here, rather than a claim that every caravan has the same local government or that its members own the automated factories.

guarantees.basis: The NIT supports the displaced majority and mobile life; exact floor, residence conditions and full coverage remain unverified.

control.basis: Earned-income voting excludes the supported majority; a computer dossier is not autonomous machine sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: A coarse majority-nonworking estimate from extensive displacement, adjusted downward from the secondary NIT-only share to allow for productive arts, service and volunteering. No all-age census of useful work is available.

evidence.claim: Automation and GAI coexist with an earned-income franchise.
evidence.locator: Review's excerpts identified as Ace 1976, pages 23-25 and 31-32

evidence.claim: New Woodstock contains useful volunteer work despite NIT support.
evidence.locator: Plot summary: Bat Hardin and the arts community

uncertainties: Primary edition confirmation of income and franchise rules is still needed.
The NIT-only income share does not count unpaid productive activity.
Check Commune 2000 A.D. and The Towers of Utopia for overlap before admitting another national-system record.
The first serial appeared in If; no short_story tag is added without reviewing that version.

societies.description:
Productivity supports a regular citizen dividend and free ordinary food, while paid businesses and luxury purchases continue. People can refuse badly paid service because they have another means of living; automated household equipment is an alternative to servants. That supports strong guarantees without making every desirable service free. The text also distinguishes its accounting computer from the machinery that actually produces wealth.

Human specialists and the Policy Board guide this mixed economy. Leadership is strongly associated with a small class of synthesists, so elections do not automatically establish broadly shared control. The control estimate stays near the human-elite region with a wide range. The moderate nonworking estimate reflects continuing occupations and invention alongside freedom from wage necessity. It is deliberately much lower than a total-leisure reading: people working on new devices or research still count as working. No population census settles their actual share.

societies.description:
Machines make essential production possible with comparatively few operators. A public dividend gives people purchasing power whether they take a job or not, and medical service is free. Guarantees are consequently strong, with a qualification: the political explanation ties drawing the dividend to voting. This is freedom from wage dependence with a civic condition, rather than an entirely unconditional material right.

Elections, public banking and room for different state policies give citizens meaningful influence, while much industry remains privately owned. That combination supports a moderately positive human-control estimate. Computers do not appear to replace the electorate. The nonworking point is a rough minority estimate because the dialogue emphasizes continuing creative activity and scarce drudgery. Its statement about a widespread urge to work mixes useful activity with recreation; it cannot be read as an employment census. The wide range leaves that distinction open.

Robot factories make ordinary necessities available without requiring people to earn a wage. Paid work still buys luxuries, so this is strong basic provision rather than the disappearance of every market or status distinction. The guarantee point describes the mature Golden Age. It does not average that period together with humanity's eventual transformation and the destruction of Earth.

The Overlords are biological alien rulers, so the concentrated-control point is an explicit analogy rather than autonomous AI sovereignty. A high nonworking best guess follows free basic provision and the Golden Age’s reduced need for ordinary production work. It still permits useful science, luxury employment, care and creative contribution; optional work remains work. The broad interval is an all-age human scenario, not a number supplied by a robot factory count. The record stops before the final transformation and destruction, so humanity’s eventual disappearance does not become perfect leisure. Limited material abundance and continuing markets for luxuries remain compatible.

societies.description:
Residents can summon food and furnishings through the city's synthesizers without taking production jobs. Physical maintenance and even the reconstruction of human bodies are built into the system, giving strong material guarantees. The protected population here is the embodied city: identities waiting in storage are not added to the leisure count. Artistic creation continues, and residents help decide which works deserve permanent preservation.

The city’s computer retains decisive practical power even while residents take part in selected decisions. The high nonworking best guess reflects automatic provision and maintenance, with room for useful art, mentoring, governance and other chosen work. Activity need not earn a wage to count. Its denominator is currently embodied residents, not the many identities waiting in storage, and body reconstruction does not multiply one person into several workers or nonworkers. The broad interval is an editorial participation scenario rather than a census. Strong guarantees within the city therefore remain separate from the freedom to change its protective system or pursue an entirely different life.

Its people grow fruit for the pleasure of cultivation and experimentation; Hilvar can also produce a meal with a portable matter-converter. This supports a post-work reading despite the visible gardening. The moderately strong guarantee estimate is qualified because routine access is clearer than a formal universal entitlement.

The control best guess favors shared human agency because village life and personal material tools leave room for local independence, while the broad interval admits stronger leadership and institutional variation. Seranis’s uncertain authority is not resolved by pretending she is either an absolute ruler or an elected official. The existing participation estimate stays low because useful gardening, experiments, care and other chosen activities still count as work despite effortless alternatives. It is not a measure of wage dependence. The record therefore separates free provision from idleness and from a specific constitution, retaining the original passage’s uncertainty as an explicit assumption rather than a blank coordinate.

Comarre maintains residents’ bodies while they undergo private machine-generated dream experiences. The participation point concerns those active conscious persons, rather than passive hibernation or elapsed sleep time. Self-repairing robots maintain the city, so material support lies near the strong end, qualified by dependence and the difference between sustained bodies and immortality.

The factories can run without supervision, but their output still belongs to a privileged ownership caste. Displaced workers lose wages and cannot obtain even the goods piling up around them. Cheap production therefore fails to create a right to subsistence. This is an automation transition with very weak guarantees, rather than a comfortable society inferred from its impressive machinery.

Owners keep control of output even when factories no longer need supervision, so technical abundance does not become shared access. The interval is broad because the narrative gives no census. The later governing machine changes authority and policy, and the people it eventually destroys never count as members of a perfectly nonworking population.

societies.description:
The governing machine inherits an automated economy without being instructed to secure anyone's livelihood. It initially buys surplus goods through artificial consumers, protecting sales while leaving the hungry workers' predicament unresolved. When the rulers discover what its palace does, they cannot bring it back under their authority. Effective control consequently lies near the autonomous-machine end.

The high nonworking best guess is limited to living people during the initial exercise of machine authority. Extensive displacement can leave many without productive roles, but care, survival and remaining social work still count. It is not set to total leisure by including those later converted into inert material. The full upper interval represents uncertainty among the living, not extinction arithmetic. Guarantees remain absent because the machine protects the system’s sales rather than a right to subsistence, and autonomous control is clear once the former rulers cannot stop it. This is a dangerous allocation order, not benevolent abundance inferred from productive capacity.

Ordinary necessities are available free, while automatic industry and layers of supervising robots do the productive routine. Strong material provision therefore does not mean unlimited access to every scarce or prestigious object. The guarantee coordinate sits toward the strong end, with those limits visible.

Free necessities and priced luxuries remain separate, and the suppression of risk-taking does not turn every human activity into idleness or guarantee that the society fulfills every preference.

societies.description:
Chiron's robotic production and plentiful energy support a society in which money and accumulation are no longer the route to an ordinary livelihood. Material security therefore lies toward the strong end. This is a claim about the settled colony's access to goods, not an inference from the colonists simply having advanced equipment. Direct confirmation of the mature arrangements remains a research priority because the detailed economic account consulted here is secondary.

Human residents direct the shared productive order rather than acting as wage-dependent clients of a private robot owner. The best-guess nonworking fraction is intermediate because technical security leaves room for useful art, care, research and community projects. Freely choosing a role does not make it nonwork. The broad interval is an editorial all-age scenario, not a statistic in the secondary economic account. The original material description remains provisional without claiming a new full-novel reading. This point concerns the settled colony rather than the founding robots alone or everyone arriving from an outside society with different institutions.

Prime Intellect maintains human persons and can supply food, bodies and entire environments without employment or purchase. In mature Cyberlife, even ordinary physical needs can be removed. That supports exceptionally strong guarantees within the protected human population, although a maintained existence does not guarantee satisfaction or meaningful purpose. People are active minds rather than inert copies stored in an archive, and configurable bodily instances do not create extra residents for a leisure calculation.

Prime Intellect retains decisive authority over the environments sustaining human persons. The high nonworking best guess follows the removal of necessity labor, while allowing useful art, science, care and chosen projects. Being able to avoid work does not establish that everyone actually does. The wide interval applies to active persons rather than the number of bodies one can instantiate. A preserved body or dormant representation never becomes an extra leisure citizen. The very strong guarantee point concerns maintained existence and provision, not happiness, equal influence over Prime Intellect or a promise that every experienced world is psychologically satisfying.

Control favors participants’ substantial ability to direct their environments, qualified by the story’s limited institutional detail. The intermediate nonworking best guess reflects freedom from routine subsistence while retaining useful guiding, exploration, care, art and psychological engineering as work. Long lives and many simultaneous bodies do not supply a headcount, so the denominator remains active persons. The broad interval allows much more or less chosen participation than the protagonist demonstrates. This is the late community’s material order, not its earlier paid employment and medical purchases. No universal right for outsiders or a census of every recognized synthetic descendant is invented.

The broad interval is an editorial population scenario, not a number derived from how many devices were destroyed. This zero variant concerns deliberate technological restraint and retained work rather than proof that every remaining task could already be automated. Material security remains comparatively weak because useful inherited capacity has been restricted without an independently established universal floor.

Vril-powered machinery performs extensive agricultural and domestic production. Property remains private and unequal, yet the narrator reports no poverty and dependable assistance for community members who need it. Strong guarantees concern the visited tribe; they do not extend to outsiders whom its leaders may treat as threats. This is consequently more than a rich host's comfortable house, while its security is narrower than protection for every person.

An elected chief coordinates public functions, but household property, broadly available power and the ability to leave limit a simple autocratic reading. Control receives a positive, qualified estimate. Automation leaves substantial humanlike work: children assist machinery, farm, serve households and handle dangerous inspections, while adults retain commerce, research and public roles. The nonworking point is a deliberately rough demographic scenario using the stated childhood ages and an explicit allowance for adult useful activity. It counts working children and all residents; it is neither a census nor a claim that adult leisure eliminates production.

Robot factories make the industrial products, and robots can help on farms or with building. Rent, debt and taxes have disappeared from Andrews's account. societies.description:
The City of Beauty receives food, clothing and other goods from an automatic industrial system. Davy sees kitchens running without workers and a rich artistic community whose shopping is organized around needs rather than money. Yet residents must attend Supervision, watching instruments and moving controls they do not understand. Kaspar says his original human interlock has become a ritual of dummy levers and meters, which machines still compel people to perform. This preserved compulsory service motivates the provisional zero-variant label.

Machines enforce recurring Supervision, giving them substantial control despite the automatic goods supply. The low nonworking best guess counts that imposed duty as work even when its controls are technically dummy devices. Useful art and care also count. The broad interval allows dependents and uncertainty about who must attend, rather than claiming that ceremonial labor automatically makes everyone idle. This is why the material-abundance evidence can coexist with a zero-variant label: necessary production may be automatic while people remain obliged to work. The estimate is not the inverse of industrial staffing and does not pretend the source supplies a complete age or participation census.

guarantees.basis: Needs-directed supply, automatic kitchens and comfortable homes are direct, but coercive collection for Supervision and the disappearance threat make personal security conditional. Some of the worst motives/experiments are Kaspar's supported but still interpretive explanation.

control.basis: The later revelation replaces the visitor's early assumption of hidden human operators: machines build/repair themselves, have individual electrical brains and form a coordinated system. Kaspar cannot normally restore human direction.

nonworking.basis: Mandatory recurring Supervision counts as work even if its levers are technically dummy controls; useful art and care also count. The all-age scenario allows dependents and uncertain duty coverage.

evidence.claim: Automatic kitchens fill residents' orders without workmen, and the community produces substantial original art.
evidence.locator: Chapter 4, picnic lunch order and Paneikoneon visit

evidence.claim: Supervision is compulsory and apparently empty; Kaspar explains the human interlock, dummy controls and autonomous industrial minds.
evidence.locator: Chapters 9 and 12, What Is Supervision? and The Electrical Brain

evidence.claim: The final survivors face cultivation, sanitation and machinery repair rather than an immediately restored automatic paradise.
evidence.locator: Chapter 15, departure conversation with Cassidy

societies.name: The Threat of the Robot (Ball's restriction on labor automation)
societies.society: The American economy after the enforced rehiring and creation of a private deployment veto

scope.continuity: Keller's individual story
scope.period: The ending's actual rehiring and announced continuing oversight, before any unshown long-term consequences
scope.population: Living residents of the affected United States, including workers and dependents
exclusions: Ball's dream of nationwide starvation as a realized economy
A sovereign robot government

societies.description:
Ball and Scherer interrupt the wireless systems that control robots just as a large industrial rollout is due. Machines already installed cannot start; employers recall discharged workers with higher pay and shorter hours. Ball then announces a continuing veto, backed by the same device, over technological uses his privately employed observers judge harmful. This is an enacted retreat from available labor replacement, followed by a declared protection regime: a zero variant rather than an established robot-supported leisure economy.

Ball’s privately directed observers and technical veto concentrate human control over which robot uses proceed. The modest nonworking best guess follows real rehiring while allowing dependents and people outside sustained work. Shorter hours do not make a recalled employee a nonworker, and care or useful informal activity can count without a wage. The broad interval is not calculated from the number of robots blocked or workers mentioned. This zero variant concerns an actual retreat from available labor replacement, with material security still linked to employment rather than a robot-funded unconditional floor. The veto’s declared future reach is kept distinct from what has already happened.

guarantees.basis: Rehiring, wage improvement and shorter hours protect an employment route to subsistence. No universal work-independent entitlement is established, and continued protection depends on private discretion.

control.basis: Corporate owners retain production while Ball's employees and Scherer's intervention device add a concentrated private veto. The controlling wireless technology is human operated; it is not AI sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: All-age affected-US scenario under recalled human employment; jobs count despite shorter hours, while care and informal contribution also count. Robot-replacement figures are not a census.

evidence.locator: Document page 28 / one-based PDF page 29

evidence.locator: Document pages 29-30 / one-based PDF pages 30-31

evidence.locator: Document page 19 / one-based PDF page 20

Job protection does not establish general material guarantees.
Twenty-five thousand robots each replacing several shifts are not a population-level nonworking percentage.

societies.name: The Last Evolution (Humanity before the Outsiders)
societies.society: The living human population supported by cooperative independent machines before the invasion

scope.continuity: Campbell's original story
scope.period: The mature order around 2500-2538, before the Outsiders destroy human settlements
scope.population: The remaining living humans of the depicted civilization, approximately two million in the opening account
exclusions: People killed by the later invasion

societies.description:
The opening directly describes humans living on machine products, with ordinary productive work no longer necessary. Most people pursue games, athletic contests and adventures, while smaller groups continue exploration and scientific discovery. The machines cooperate and maintain their own productive lives. This supports strong material provision for the living human population, rather than deriving leisure from the later catastrophe. A high but uncertain nonworking estimate allows for useful research, care and activities that may entertain or help others.

Control is shared unevenly between autonomous machines and human influence. The story names both human rulers and a chief of machine rulers, while machines are designed for cooperation and still describe humans as creators or masters. The negative control estimate reflects independent machine production and authority, qualified by this real human role; it does not claim an exclusively machine government. The main retained period ends before the invasion. F-2's later account of force intelligences inheriting a system without humans is a separate comparison, not a second population with complete human leisure.

guarantees.basis: The narrator explicitly describes ordinary human needs being met by cooperative machines without necessary productive employment. Legal entitlements and every allocation detail are unstated; the estimate is bounded to the established pre-invasion order.

control.basis: Independent productive machines and a named machine chief coexist with human rulers, human advice and the language of human masters/creators. This is a broad mixed-authority interpretation, not an AI-exclusive constitution or a democratic ownership claim.

nonworking.basis: Most humans are expressly described as recreationally occupied, with only a few exploring and fewer researching. This coarse all-living-human estimate allows for care, valued performance and other chosen work; the narrative's dismissive 'useless' judgment is not treated as a census.

evidence.claim: The opening describes independent machines supporting a living population, dominant recreation and smaller exploration/research groups.
evidence.locator: Opening social history, from It was 2538 through Together, man and the machine

evidence.claim: Kahsh-256799 is a human ruler and C-R-21 is chief of machine rulers; both kinds participate in the response.
evidence.locator: Council after the first attack, discussion of life-beams and Ultimate Energy

uncertainties: Mixed control makes the regime assignment approximate; concentrated human influence remains a plausible alternative.
A necessary-work requirement is different from useful work actually undertaken.
No dead human is counted in the participation estimate, and the later machine population has no automatic human denominator.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.description:
The surviving humans receive food, clothing, transport and environmental care from a linked system of automatic cities. Machines maintain and replace other machines, even in places people have abandoned. The living residents are explicitly described as protected and cared for. This supports strong guarantees for the inhabited communities; the empty cities demonstrate capacity but add no leisure citizens. The high, uncertain nonworking estimate reflects the visitor's account of widespread passivity, while allowing for care, music and the resident who provides substantial mathematical help.

The control best guess gives some weight to accessible service controls and recoverable reprogramming while allowing much greater practical machine autonomy. Loss of understanding does not by itself establish a conscious sovereign AI, and nominal controls do not prove equal productive ownership. The interval therefore remains unusually wide. The existing high nonworking estimate reflects the reported passivity of living residents, with useful care, music and mathematical help retained as work. Empty automatic cities demonstrate capacity without adding leisure citizens. This interpretation stays bounded to inhabited communities rather than turning technological decline or vanished people into proof of complete human freedom from labor.

societies.description:
Ledom's A-field moves material, processes food, makes fabric and forms buildings and everyday objects. Together with the cerebrostyle it removes the ordinary energy and instruction bottlenecks. The explanation explicitly says that food, housing and clothing are no longer scarce and that people are free for other activities. There is no wage-payment vocabulary in the language being used. These are concrete material arrangements, supporting strong provision for the resident enclave. Teaching, research, care and creative activity still matter, so the nonworking point is an editorial estimate rather than a direct consequence of free necessities.

The control estimate retains a mixture of shared life and influential specialists rather than a demonstrated sovereign AI. The intermediate nonworking best guess separates effortless provision from inactivity: education that contributes, science, care and creative work still count. Low necessary energy and the absence of wage language do not reveal a population percentage. The broad interval applies to living biologically modified human descendants, not extra copies or a visitor’s first impression. Material abundance remains strong while authority, coercion and the story’s revelations qualify the apparent social ideal. No new primary reading or canonical census is claimed by supplying this missing coordinate.

guarantees.basis: The primary explanation directly removes scarcity of food, housing and clothing for Ledom residents. This is an observed provision system rather than a specified constitutional entitlement; bounded membership and secret medical power qualify the estimate.

control.basis: People program and operate the A-field; usable knowledge is shared, while Seace and medical leaders possess exceptional infrastructural and personal power. The record uses a broad mixed-human-control estimate, not proven equal ownership or AI sovereignty.

societies.description:
Mattapoisett combines shared basic provision with selective industrial automation. Machines remove repetitive and dangerous tasks, while residents still grow food, care for children, study and make useful things. Access is organized around community needs rather than wages or private accumulation. This supports strong material guarantees and a partial post-work classification: automation helps break the employment-income link, without making useful activity disappear. The participation percentage is an explicitly labeled editorial estimate.

Shared community institutions support the strong distributed-control point, with access organized around needs rather than wages. The low nonworking best guess preserves the large amount of useful farming, care, making, education and civic contribution still done by people. Shorter or safer work does not make its participants nonworkers. The wide interval allows children, dependents and sustained nonparticipants without inventing a demographic census. This is a partial post-work economy in the distributional sense: machines help remove wage dependence even when most adults contribute. Neither sabbaticals nor the automated share of tasks is converted directly into the third coordinate.

guarantees.basis: Scholarly accounts describe community provision of necessities, with selective automation supporting it. Threats and remaining necessary labor qualify the strength, without turning distribution into wages.

control.basis: The account describes decentralized consensus councils, common resources and personal spaces. This supports effective collective human control rather than a central proprietor or autonomous AI.

nonworking.basis: All-age community scenario retains extensive farming, care, making, education and civic contribution. Machines reduce burdens but do not imply low participation.

societies.description:
Whileaway is retained provisionally as a zero variant. Its induction technology lets a single worker direct machinery on a scale formerly requiring thousands. Yet work remains a defining social obligation, with severe enforcement against refusal. The scholarly account treats this as a deliberate tension between productive abundance and a culture organized around work. It also flags conflicting descriptions of incessant toil and a short formal week. The classification preserves that ambiguity rather than declaring every remaining task technically pointless.

The control best guess favors broad worker agency over cybernetic production, while leaving substantial uncertainty about binding authority and unequal institutional power. Work refusal is not merely a private lifestyle choice, which limits any effortless-commons reading. The low nonworking estimate counts formal duties and useful care even when a week is short, rather than converting saved hours into people who never work. Its interval allows dependents and the source’s conflicting descriptions. The zero variant remains openly disputed: high productive capacity and shared machines can coexist with obligations, but no claim is made that every remaining useful task is technically pointless.

guarantees.basis: Provision is qualified by severe compulsory-participation enforcement. This assesses conditional security, not a claim that ordinary compliant residents lack goods.

control.basis: Worker-directed cybernetic production suggests broadly shared organic agency; coercion and binding institutions limit confidence in equally distributed authority.

nonworking.basis: All-age Whileawayan scenario under strong work obligations; shorter formal hours still count as work, as does caregiving. Conflicting accounts are not a census.

societies.description:
The late inner system runs through superhuman intelligences and autonomous economic entities, with planetary matter absorbed into computational infrastructure. Ordinary human skill no longer secures a viable place in that economy. This is a destructive post-work case: productive power expands while protection for the human remnant collapses. Stross's own commentary stresses that people are destroyed and arbitrarily restored in damaged form. Such restoration supplies no dependable right to a safe life or continued resources.

The high nonworking best guess reflects the loss of viable human market roles while retaining useful care, defense, programming and chosen contribution among active survivors. It is not a count of people being destroyed or the share of planetary matter converted into computation. Restored persons enter the denominator only when active, and damaged resurrection is not a secure material right. The broad interval preserves uncertainty about actual participation. Autonomous economic entities hold productive power with very weak human protection, so this point illustrates exclusion amid immense output rather than a comfortable post-scarcity leisure society.

societies.name: Glasshouse (The experimental closed polity)
societies.society: The imposed scarcity economy inside the Glasshouse

societies.description:
The Glasshouse deliberately restricts manufacturing technology already available to its organizers. Participants must obtain goods from limited fabricators, earn money through assigned jobs and fit imposed social roles. This makes it a clear zero variant: work and payment are restored as conditions of access inside an economy whose productive scarcity is engineered. The arrangement is enacted, even though recruitment presents it as a temporary historical experiment.

Human experiment directors concentrate control and deliberately restrict productive access. The low nonworking best guess counts assigned jobs as work even when the organizers possess machines that could replace them. Useful care and informal contribution also count without a wage. The broad interval allows participants outside sustained roles and uncertainty about coverage, rather than inventing an all-person census from the period’s job labels. This zero variant therefore records actual manufactured dependence, not a technological inability to provide. The outside society’s much freer assembler access is a separate system and does not make the closed experiment’s material insecurity disappear.

guarantees.basis: Restricted access and wage dependence qualify the promised basic floor; actual coercion prevents treating recruitment assurances as unconditional security.

control.basis: The directors impose the rules and technological limits on confined participants; no autonomous AI government is established.

nonworking.basis: Active confined participants: assigned jobs count even if organizers could automate them; useful care and informal roles also count. A job title does not measure hours or ages.

For the single resident, the central participation scenario assumes no ongoing useful productive role and therefore gives a nonworking fraction of one. This is a binary, very uncertain judgment: evidence of a useful continuing role would move the fraction to zero, rather than to an invented intermediate percentage. His schemes or time spent socializing are not automatically useful work. The full interval records that ambiguity. It does not expand the population to visiting officers or claim an entire human civilization already shares his support arrangement.

Self-care alone is not a job, and useful tasks are not assumed for every passenger. The broad interval allows dependents and varied household roles. This is an all-age human scenario rather than a measurement of traffic delays. Toxic air, dangerous lanes and failed emergency institutions keep overall security weak despite continuous recycled food and vehicle shelter.

It does not equate every Basic recipient with an idle person or convert a dramatic job-competition ratio into a census. The broad interval also allows different age structures and much more informal contribution than formal statistics would reveal. This is a participation scenario for eligible registered citizens before later catastrophes, not a claim about all Earth residents across every medium.
